cita: Liang et al. (2024). SAGE: Self-evolving Agents with Reflective and Memory-augmented Abilities.
problema: LLM agents in dynamic environments must continuously make decisions and adapt, but they lack long-term memory mechanisms and are limited by short context windows; multi-agent frameworks that try to compensate incur heavy communication overhead and rising resource demands as interaction history grows.
mecanismo: A three-agent loop (User, Assistant, Checker) iteratively refines the assistant's policy via checker feedback; the assistant reflects on observations/actions to derive self-reflections stored in Long-Term Memory (WRITE); a dual Short-Term/Long-Term Memory system is governed by 'MemorySyntax', which combines the Ebbinghaus forgetting-curve retention-rate model with linguistic optimization of each information item's strength, applying threshold rules to keep an item in STM, transfer it to LTM, or discard it (CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION).
evaluacion: AgentBench (OS/DB/KG/ALFWorld/WebShop/Mind2Web) with GPT-3.5/GPT-4 and open-source backbones (Llama2/CodeLlama/Qwen/ChatGLM2); long-form QA, multi-turn dialogue and sequential-task benchmarks; long-context code/reasoning tasks (LCC, RepoBench-P, HotpotQA, TriviaQA) vs Beam Search and Reflexion; a RAG-agent comparison (BM25/DPR/OpenAI-Retrieval/TART/FiD) on accuracy, latency and memory usage; a memory-optimization ablation on Qwen-1.8B and CodeLlama-7B.
numeros_clave: AgentBench Database task up to 2.26x improvement on closed-source models, 57.7%-100% on open-source models (Abstract); ChatGPT-4-SAGE RAG variant cuts memory usage ~50% and improves accuracy 3.6%-4.7% without added latency (Table 4); ablation: Qwen-1.8B KG task improves 6.8->45.3 with memory optimization (Table 5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MemorySyntax's retention-rate threshold rule for keep/discard/transfer between STM and LTM (Sec 3.2.2, Eq.10-12) is a concrete formalized consolidation policy MF could adapt for promoting or pruning gotchas.

The RAG-agent comparison shows SAGE cuts memory usage ~50% while improving accuracy without added latency (Table 4), evidencing that structured memory design can win on the cost axis, not just quality.

The Ebbinghaus-based forgetting selectively discards low-retention information by design (Sec 3.2.2), a staleness-management policy relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor, but the paper does not measure resulting factual drift or poisoning directly.

notes: Numbers Table 1 (AgentBench), Table 4 (RAG agents latency/memory), Table 5 (ablation). plan_estado=NO.

cita: Li, Jing & Jing (2024). Vector Storage Based Long-term Memory Research on LLM.
problema: LLM agents face high reasoning cost and low decision quality on complex, multi-round tasks because a limited context window causes semantic loss of earlier task and dialogue history, undermining coherence and reasoning efficiency.
mecanismo: Historical interaction data (knowledge, dialog, task) is sliced, embedded (ColBERT) and stored as three separately-typed memory banks in a vector database (dense FAISS index) plus a sparse Elasticsearch/BM25 keyword index (WRITE, HIBRIDA representation); an evaluation strategy tags stored experiences as positive/negative or relevant/irrelevant/conflicting before admission (ADMISION); retrieval blends dense cosine-similarity search with sparse BM25 and adds a recency/time-decay weight per memory type; an Ebbinghaus forgetting-curve model with a per-segment forgetting-rate parameter (reset on each retrieval hit) prunes memory segments over time (ACTUALIZACION/OLVIDO).
evaluacion: ALFWorld, HotpotQA and KAgentBench multi-task datasets with chatglm3-6b and Qwen2-7b (ChatGPT used to augment data), comparing NoAgent/ReAct/InterAct baselines against VIMBank on task success rate (EM/LCS-based metrics) and reasoning cost.
numeros_clave: Success rate of task decision increased by 10%-20% and reasoning cost reduced by about 23% overall (Abstract); reasoning cost reduced by nearly 25% as tasks execute (Sec V); decision accuracy improves >10% vs InterAct and >20% vs NoAgent (Conclusion).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Task memory explicitly stores the LLM's strategic-planning process (task planning, tool selection, observations) as retrievable state that guides subsequent rounds (Sec III.A.2/B), directly relevant to MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor.

VIMBank splits memory into three typed, separately-retrieved banks (knowledge/dialog/task) with per-type retrieval strategies (Sec III.C), a concrete single-source-per-fact-type seam pattern MF's COSTURAS anchor could reuse.
The paper directly measures and reports a ~23-25% reasoning-cost reduction from the memory mechanism (Abstract, Sec V), supporting MF's cost/latency lens.

notes: Numbers in Abstract + Sec V (cost reduction) + Conclusion (accuracy deltas). plan_estado=SI justified by the task-memory/planning module (Sec III.A.2).

cita: Liu et al. (2024). Memory-Augmented Agent Training for Business Document Understanding.
problema: Enterprises still process business documents like invoices manually because directly applying general-purpose LLMs to specialized business-document extraction (e.g. transport-reference extraction) yields unsatisfactory results, and agents lack a systematic way to distill and reuse strategic insights across repeated document-reasoning attempts.
mecanismo: A long-term memory M is trained by sampling mini-batches of task trajectories over the training set (WRITE); after each trajectory, a Reflector LLM post-hoc labels it correct/incorrect and pinpoints which reasoning steps succeeded or failed (ACTUALIZACION); a meta-optimizer LLM then ingests the trajectories, their reflector assessments, and the CURRENT memory to progressively rewrite the memory into distilled, generalizable heuristics -- not raw responses or plain summaries -- that guide future task-solving attempts (CONSOLIDACION).
evaluacion: A real-world UBL invoice transport-reference-extraction dataset from a logistics partner (open-sourced anonymized subset), comparing chain-of-thought prompting, a vanilla LLM agent, and Reflexion baselines; separate analysis of average API calls, average cost, and successfully-solved document length across optimization epochs (gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini backbones).
numeros_clave: Matrix outperforms single-LLM CoT prompting by 30.3%, vanilla LLM agent by 35.2%, and Reflexion by 27.28% (Abstract/Intro); average API calls reduced ~8.12% (gpt-4o) and ~21.3% (gpt-4o-mini) after memory optimization (Sec 4, Fig.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The meta-optimizer explicitly rewrites memory into distilled, generalizable heuristics rather than storing raw trajectories or simple summaries (Sec 3.2, 'Optimization'), directly matching MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor of promoting gotchas into durable recipes.
The paper directly measures API-call and cost reduction as memory optimization proceeds (Sec 4, Fig.4/5), a concrete cost/latency signal supporting MF's COSTO anchor.

Memory writes happen once per training epoch via a fixed reflect-then-optimize schedule rather than a discretionary in-task trigger (Sec 3.2), so it only partially informs MF's G-M1 write-trigger question.

notes: Numbers from Abstract + Sec 4 ('Analysis of the Optimized System', Fig.4, Table 1). plan_estado=NO.

cita: Li et al. (2025). Cogito, ergo sum: A Neurobiologically-Inspired Cognition-Memory-Growth System for Code Generation.
problema: Existing multi-agent code-generation pipelines follow a fixed plan-then-code-then-debug workflow that mirrors a textbook process rather than human learning, and incur high inter-agent communication costs, while existing external-memory designs either store full raw responses (excessive space) or summarize everything (losing detail).
mecanismo: A single 'Super-Role' agent rotates in reverse order through Debugger->Coder->Planner roles, each stage writing its output into a hippocampus-inspired memory module with four dedicated regions (DG=new-memory intake, CA1=long-term store of initial responses, CA2=user-personalization store, CA3=fast-recall of code-version+error-traceback pairs, CA4=bridge storing only the final correct/most-recent tokenized result); each candidate answer receives an importance score (quality x role-weight) that determines how strongly it is retained (CONSOLIDACION), and accumulated cross-stage experience is retrieved to inform the next stage, ultimately producing one Super-Role answer.
evaluacion: 8 code-generation benchmarks (HumanEval, HumanEval-ET, EvalPlus, MBPP, MBPP-ET, APPS, xCodeEval, CodeContest) with GPT-3.5-turbo/GPT-4, vs Direct/CoT/Self-Planning/Analogical/Reflexion/Self-Collaboration/MapCoder baselines using Pass@k; a dedicated API-call/token-consumption table; an ablation removing Planning/Implementation/Debugging experience and the Super-Role itself.
numeros_clave: Vs MapCoder (GPT-3.5-turbo): +12.1% HumanEval, +16.6% HumanEval-ET, +59.29% APPS (Table 1); token consumption reduced up to 66.29% and API calls up to 70% on HumanEval, average token reduction 32.81% / API-call reduction 28.46% (Sec 4.2, Table 2); ablation: removing Planning experience causes up to 14.02% performance drop (Sec 4.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The importance-score-weighted retention of candidate answers per hippocampus region (Sec 3.4) is a concrete, quantitative gate for what gets consolidated into durable memory that MF could adapt.

The 4-region hippocampus split (initial answers / personalization / code+error pairs / final-correct-result) is a typed single-purpose-per-region memory design (Sec 3.3) directly resonant with MF's COSTURAS single-source-per-fact concern.
The paper directly measures and reports token/API-call reduction from its reversed workflow and memory design (Table 2), reinforcing MF's cost/latency lens.

notes: Numbers Table 1 (Pass@k deltas), Table 2 (API calls/tokens), Sec 4.3 (ablation). plan_estado=NO.

cita: Xu et al. (2025). A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents.
problema: Current LLM-agent memory systems provide only basic storage/retrieval with fixed, predefined operations and structures -- even graph-database-backed ones like Mem0 -- so they cannot flexibly reorganize or form new connections as knowledge evolves, limiting adaptability and long-term interaction quality.
mecanismo: Zettelkasten-inspired: each new interaction becomes a structured atomic 'note' with LLM-generated keywords/tags/contextual description plus a dense embedding (WRITE, HIBRIDA representation); link generation retrieves the top-k most similar existing notes by embedding similarity and prompts an LLM to decide which connections are meaningful, updating a link graph; the same LLM call can also rewrite the context, keywords and tags of the retrieved neighboring notes so the whole network's understanding deepens as new memories arrive (CONSOLIDACION/ACTUALIZACION, 'memory evolution'); retrieval is dense cosine-similarity top-k over note embeddings, automatically pulling in linked notes.
evaluacion: LoCoMo (long multi-session QA, 7,512 QA pairs, up to 35 sessions) and DialSim (TV-show-derived long-term multi-party dialogue QA) across six foundation models (Llama3.2-1b/3b, Qwen2.5-1.5b, GPT-4o/4o-mini) vs LoCoMo/ReadAgent/MemoryBank/MemGPT baselines, F1/BLEU-1/ROUGE/METEOR/SBERT metrics; an ablation removing Link Generation and Memory Evolution; a hyperparameter sweep over top-k.
numeros_clave: DialSim F1 3.45 vs LoCoMo baseline 2.55 (+35%) and MemGPT 1.18 (+192%) (Table 2); ~1,200 tokens per memory operation, 85-93% token reduction vs baselines' ~16,900 tokens, cost <$0.0003/op, 5.4s (GPT-4o-mini) / 1.1s (local Llama3.2-1b) per operation (Sec 4.3); ablation: removing Link Generation+Memory Evolution drops Multi-Hop F1 from 27.02 to 9.65 (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Memory evolution -- new notes triggering rewrites of neighboring notes' context/keywords/tags (Sec 3.3, Eq.7) -- is a concrete mechanism for continuously refining durable memory content that MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt.

The paper directly measures and reports an 85-93% token reduction and sub-cent per-operation cost vs full-history baselines (Sec 4.3 'Cost-Efficiency Analysis'), a strong quantified instance of MF's cost/latency concern.
The link graph built from embedding-similarity plus LLM-judged connections (Sec 3.2) is a derived index over raw notes, analogous to MF's Tier-3 derived-index/cache concept.

cita: Xu, D., Wen, Y., Jia, P., Zhang, Y., Zhang, W., Wang, Y., Guo, H., Tang, R., Zhao, X., Chen, E. y Xu, T. (2025). From Single to Multi-Granularity: Toward Long-Term Memory Association and Selection of Conversational Agents.
problema: Existing retrieval-augmented conversational memory systems depend on single-granularity segmentation and retrieval (session, turn, or summary alone), which fails to capture deep cross-granularity connections between memories, causing partial retrieval of useful information or excessive noise on multi-session queries.
mecanismo: Each session is processed by an LLM into multiple granularity units -- session, turn, summary, keyword -- (WRITE); a Gaussian Mixture Model clusters the new memory's similarity vector against historical memories into an accept/reject set, and only accepted (similar) memories are linked into a persistent association graph, mimicking selective memory consolidation (CONSOLIDACION); an entropy-based router computes per-granularity retrieval confidence (Shannon entropy of the similarity distribution) and assigns soft weights, then Personalized PageRank ranks candidate memory nodes using these weights, and a final LLM pass filters redundant/irrelevant retrieved content before response generation.
evaluacion: 4 long-term memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, Long-MT-Bench+, LongMemEval-s, LongMemEval-m) with GPT-4o-mini, against Full-History, MPNet/Contriever retrievers, RecurSum, MPC, A-Mem, SeCom, HippoRAG2, RAPTOR baselines; F1/BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore/GPT4o-as-Judge for QA and Recall@k/NDCG@k for retrieval; an ablation removing GMM, PPR, the granularity router, and the whole Memory Association step; token/latency cost reporting.
numeros_clave: MemGAS F1 60.20 on LongMemEval-s vs next-best HippoRAG2 57.60 (Table 1); Recall@10 94.47 on LongMemEval-s vs HippoRAG2 91.28 (Table 2); ablation (w/o Memory Association) drops GPT4o-J from 60.20 to 55.40 on LongMemEval-s (Table 3), while average tokens/latency stay close to lightweight retrievers (8,829 tokens, 2.55s).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The multi-granularity memory units (session/turn/summary/keyword) plus the association graph form exactly a layered derived-index structure MF's TIER-INDICE anchor targets, with an explicit accept/reject gate on what gets indexed (Sec 2.2).

Retrieval granularity is chosen per-query via a measured entropy signal rather than a fixed heuristic (Sec 2.3), and the paper reports Recall@k/NDCG@k directly (Table 2), strongly aligning with MF's G-M2 measured-retrieval requirement.

MemGAS reports token/latency overhead explicitly and shows it stays competitive with lightweight retrievers despite added structure (Table 1 last columns), supporting MF's cost lens on retrieval design decisions.
